response.reasoning:
Here is how I read this case. The record of the purchase describes four retired sets as "used - like new" with "boxes in good condition", and before buying, the buyer asked specifically about the boxes and was told they had been stored in a cupboard since new and were fine (lst-1, msg-1, msg-2). That makes the condition of the boxes part of what was promised, not a detail.

The parcel was delivered on 28 August at 13:49 and the buyer said something was wrong the same afternoon, a couple of hours later (trk-7, msg-3). That quick complaint makes it unlikely the damage arose in the buyer's own handling.

The photographs point the same way. The outer carton is shown intact, taped, squared-up and marked fragile, with no crushing, puncture or corner collapse (pho-1). The inner set box, by contrast, shows a clearly crushed and opened top corner along with scuffing to the edges (pho-2). An undamaged outer carton with a crushed item inside is hard to explain as a knock in transit; it fits better with the box already being in that state when it was packed, or with too little protection inside. Either way that sits on the seller's side rather than the buyer's, and it is inconsistent with "boxes in good condition". I accept the seller believes the packing was careful, but the two photographs together are the best evidence available of what actually arrived, and they are not consistent with what was described.

Against that, this is not a total failure. The photographs show damage to one box out of four sets, and there is no suggestion the sets themselves are incomplete or unusable. The buyer keeps everything that was sent. The fair measure is the loss in value from one box falling short of the description, in a purchase where box condition was expressly a significant part of the price. Thirty per cent of the money being held to the buyer, with the remaining seventy to the seller, reflects one box of four being materially worse than promised while recognising the buyer retains all four sets.

findings.statement: The item was described as "used - like new" with "boxes in good condition", and the seller confirmed in writing before the sale that the boxes were fine, after the buyer said box condition was most of what they were paying for.
The parcel was delivered on 28 August at 13:49 and the buyer said something was wrong about two and a half hours later, on the same day.
The photograph of the shipping carton shows it intact, sealed and marked fragile, with no visible crushing or impact damage to the outside.
The photograph of the set box shows a crushed and opened top corner and scuffing along the edges, which does not match "boxes in good condition".
An undamaged outer carton containing a crushed inner box points to the condition existing before shipping or to insufficient internal protection, rather than to rough handling by the carrier.
The damage evidenced concerns one box out of four sets, and there is no evidence that the sets themselves are incomplete or unusable.
